key_insight: PINNs fail on airfoil shocks because steady Euler residuals are too weak, so the optimizer prefers smooth solutions; the paper fixes this by enforcing shock formation through pseudo-time evolution toward steady state.
engineering_relevance: This makes PINNs more viable for transonic/inviscid airfoil analysis where accurate shock prediction matters for aerodynamic design and performance estimation.
method: Reformulate steady shock capturing as an unsteady Euler evolution problem.
Add time-derivative terms and a pseudo time-stepping PDE loss to guide shocks to emerge gradually.
Use a simplified Euler formulation to improve shock-capturing accuracy.
evidence_signal: The method is validated on four forward problems with different flow conditions and airfoil geometries.
watch_item: The approach still depends on solving long pseudo-time dynamics, which may be costly and sensitive to training stability or PDE-loss design.
paper_title: Physics-informed neural networks for shock capturing in inviscid flows around an airfoil
